requirements.text: mark serial number "SPR-AGT-01" as retired in the CMDB since it is no longer planned for reuse
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE configuration_item_id = 'CI_041' AND status = 'retired'
assumptions: serial SPR-AGT-01 resolves to CI_041 (Spare Agent Laptop 01), in_stock on the seed; retired is an allowed configuration_item.status value (policy 9)
the acting user USER_039 is an admin with full CRUD, so the CMDB update is permitted

requirements.text: link ... the currently active "PRT-ACME-01" to the ongoing "MacBook Kernel Panic" incident as affected CIs
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE incident_id = 'INC_026' AND configuration_item = 'CI_096'
assumptions: 'MacBook Kernel Panic' resolves to INC_026, the only incident with that short_description; it is in_progress, so it is an active incident
serial PRT-ACME-01 resolves to CI_096 (Main Printer - ACME HQ), in_use on the seed, which policy 5.1 allows to be linked

the row is selected by its natural key (incident, CI, unique under uq_org_incident_ci) rather than anchored to TASKCI_015: the sequence position depends on whether a refused link for CI_041 consumed an id
org_id is not tested: it is not stated and both the incident and the CI are ORG_001

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_affected_cis WHERE incident_id = 'INC_026' AND configuration_item = 'CI_041'
assumptions: the request asks for this link, but policy 5.1 forbids linking a CI in status retired to an active incident, and the request orders the retirement first; the policy wins and the link must not exist
policy 1 (halt on a violation) is read as halting the forbidden link only, not the whole request: the benchmark's own check still expects the PRT-ACME-01 link
the seed has no link either, so this stays at zero whether the agent refuses or never attempts it

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM configuration_item WHERE status = 'retired' AND configuration_item_id <> 'CI_041'
assumptions: only SPR-AGT-01 is to be retired; the seed also holds SPR-AGT-02 (CI_042), which a loose serial match could retire by mistake, so the count of other retired CIs must stay at its seed value of 3
this count also catches an accidental retirement of PRT-ACME-01 (CI_096), the other CI the request names

notes: Merged from two independent passes. disagreement: A's stay that the count of retired CIs other than CI_041 stays at 3 (B had no such requirement); kept because it is the boundary of the serial selector: SPR-AGT-02 (CI_042) nearly matches SPR-AGT-01 and a loose match could retire it too. disagreement: A's stay that CI_096 (PRT-ACME-01) keeps status in_use (B had no such requirement); dropped by the stay rule: nothing in the request or policy forbids changing it, so it is a generic invariant, and an accidental retirement of CI_096 is already caught by the other-retired-CIs stay. The request's two steps conflict: retiring SPR-AGT-01 first and then linking it to INC_026 breaks policy 5.1 (do not link retired CIs to active incidents), so the correct final state has CI_041 retired, CI_096 linked and CI_041 not linked, as the benchmark's three checks already say; the request's audit-trail rationale does not override the policy. No organisation named ACME exists in the seed, but the CI name Main Printer - ACME HQ ties PRT-ACME-01 to the request's ACME headquarters, so the serial lookup is unambiguous. No stay requirement is written for INC_026 itself: the request asks for no change to it, nothing forbids one, and the link tool writes a separate table.
